sources.entry: markdownify - Convert HTML to Markdown, with customizable tag handling.

summary.one_liner: A Python library that converts HTML into Markdown, with options to control which tags are stripped or converted and how headings, lists, links, and code are rendered.
summary.what_it_does: Converts HTML strings, files, or BeautifulSoup objects into Markdown through a Python function (markdownify) or a MarkdownConverter class. You can choose tags to strip or to convert, but not both. Options control link style (autolinks, default_title), heading style (ATX, ATX_CLOSED, SETEXT/UNDERLINED), bullet characters, emphasis symbol, newline style (two spaces or backslash), and whether asterisks, underscores, or other punctuation are escaped. It also handles code blocks (a fixed language or one extracted by a callback), inline images inside headings or table cells, table header inference, and optional text wrapping. Subclassing MarkdownConverter and defining convert_<tag> methods lets you customize the output for specific tags. A command-line tool is included that reads a file or stdin.
use_cases: convert a saved HTML page to Markdown
scrape web pages and store them as Markdown
clean HTML before feeding it to an LLM or notes app
custom conversion rules for specific HTML tags
batch convert HTML files from the command line
produce Markdown tables from HTML tables
how_to_run: from markdownify import markdownify as md; md('Yay GitHub')
notable: Option to strip or convert specific tags, with a choice of ATX, setext, or underlined headings
Extensible via subclassing MarkdownConverter and defining convert_<tag> methods
Code language can be extracted from pre tags with a user-supplied callback
Command-line interface that accepts files or stdin
caveats: The README does not state any limitations; the library relies on BeautifulSoup for HTML parsing
strip and convert options cannot be used together
